title: Unital shift-compatible unbounded etale compact-support projection
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ is assumed. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. On the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F=Rr_*j_!$.

Use derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], its signed symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym] and exact inverse image $f^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every unbounded $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the canonical composite
$$P_{L,K}:L\otimes_C^L Rr_*j_!K\longrightarrow Rr_*(r^*L\otimes_C^L j_!K)\longrightarrow Rr_*j_!(j^*r^*L\otimes_C^L K)=F(f^*L\otimes_C^L K)$$
is a natural isomorphism on the derived categories, independent of resolutions. The first arrow is the proper counit projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] with the signed symmetries putting $L$ first; the second is induced by the canonical sheaf extension-by-zero tensor map [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Give all functors their canonical cochain integer-shift comparisons. For fixed $K$, write $A_K(L)=L\otimes_C^L FK$, $B_K(L)=F(f^*L\otimes_C^L K)$ and $c_{H,n,L}:H(L[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(L)[n]$. Then
$$c_{B_K,n,L}\circ P_{L[n],K}=P_{L,K}[n]\circ c_{A_K,n,L}$$
for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, and $P_{C_Y,K}=1_{FK}$ under the tensor-unit identifications. For every $V\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its termwise constant complex $V_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] satisfies $f^*V_Y\cong V_X$ canonically, compatibly with shifts and units. The specialization $P_{V_Y,K}$, including its inverse, has the same coefficient-shift and unit properties.

proof.text: Apply the proved proper torsion projection formula to c.g (a finite ring is additively torsion). Each component of the compactification projection is its proper projection followed by the inverse open tensor comparison and the pullback-composition isomorphism. The two signed symmetries are isomorphisms. Thus supportProjectionMap is an isomorphism of bifunctors.

Use the existing compactification projection CommShift instance. The canonical signed symmetry commutes with the second-to-first tensor shift comparison by lem-pur-derived-tensor-braiding-shift. Whisker and compose these transformations; the inverse has CommShift because the map is an isomorphism.

Apply compactificationProjectionMap_rightUnitality. Naturality of the braiding moves the inverse-image unit comparison past the swap, and braiding_leftUnitor changes the resulting composite into the right unitor. Cancel the initial inverse swap. This proves the specified coefficient-first unit equation; multiplying by the inverse component proves its inverse equation.

The exact-functor derived comparisons have CommShift, so their composite constantFunctorCompLeftDerivedUpperStarIso and its inverse have CommShift. At the coefficient unit, the adjunction constantSheafAdj evaluated at any terminal object has unit equal to the sheafification unit. Adjunction uniqueness and the monoidal pushforward unit identity identify constantSheafCompUpperStarIso at the unit with the monoidal pullback unit map.

Apply derived_single_constants_comparison to descend the preceding unit calculation. Naturality of leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory and the proved leftDerivedUpperStar_map_singleFunctorObjUnitIso_inv_comp identify the composite with leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso. Restrict the projection and its inverse along the exact constant functor; whiskering preserves CommShift. Assemble the isomorphism and all conjuncts. Package the same shift/unit conjunction by BifunctorProjectionCoherent and apply bifunctorIsoCoherence, avoiding repeated specialization of inverse cancellation. Apply the generic coherence theorem first to an abstract map with the given forward equations, then specialize it to supportProjectionMap; a proved predicate equivalence transports the result to the declared SupportProjectionCoherent.
